llm.summary: This skill is a local note-taking and review aid for agent learnings, with its file access disclosed and limited to a project `.learnings/` folder.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to record lessons, errors, best practices, reviews, and improvement suggestions; the documented capabilities fit that purpose and are limited to local markdown records.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Some trigger phrases are conversational and could be invoked casually, but the skill repeatedly requires showing proposed content before writes and requires double confirmation before clearing records.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown documentation and a license only; no executable scripts, hooks, binary requirements, or environment variables are declared.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime access is proportionate: it reads and writes only `.learnings/` files in the current project and explicitly disclaims network upload, cross-session access, system-file modification, and automatic execution.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent local memory files and can clear them, but this persistence is core to the purpose, disclosed, scoped, and gated by confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing, be aware that the skill keeps local learning notes in each project's `.learnings/` directory. Use explicit wording when asking it to record, review, improve, score, or clear records, and review the proposed text before confirming any write or deletion.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger wording is present in README.md and SKILL.md, but the artifact-backed behavior is confined to `.learnings/` and requires user confirmation before state changes, so this is a usability/scoping caution rather than a Review-level concern.
